summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would restrict pharmaceutical company payments and benefits to doctors and require public reporting identifying practitioners who receive specified payments or other benefits.
Companies would face limits on overseas educational events, attendance costs and hospitality, alongside annual reporting of payment amounts, recipients, dates and reasons.
The inducement offences would apply from 1 January 2014, with exceptions for company representatives’ attendance costs and specified employees’ remuneration under the reporting rules.
changes: Companies could not sponsor overseas educational events aimed primarily at Australian doctors.
Catering and entertainment at covered events would be limited to $100 per person unless regulations prescribed a higher amount.
Public reports would include gifts worth more than $25 and individually name the receiving doctors.
Failure to provide the required report would attract a penalty of 3,000 penalty units.
summary.affected: Pharmaceutical companies and registered medical practitioners receiving covered payments, gifts or hospitality are affected.

speeches.speaker: Richard Di Natale
speeches.brief: The speaker moved to introduce the Therapeutic Goods Amendment (Pharmaceutical Transparency) Bill 2013, which amends the Therapeutic Goods Act 1989 to increase transparency in pharmaceutical regulation.
